title: CyberAlchemy Ontology Product Thesis
problem: Project meaning is scattered across source artifacts and one-off projections without one durable, typed, source-bound, independently validatable product contract.
value_proposition: The CyberAlchemy Ontology Product helps a project keep its meaning connected, explicit, testable, and usable while the project remains the owner of that meaning.
value_mechanism: Bind owner-selected sources exactly, preserve typed nodes and relations with explicit confidence and residue, validate deterministic package identity, and expose bounded logical retrieval for people and machines.
boundaries: ontology validation does not promote claims
Project and Goal progress does not imply achievement
runtime evidence does not prove product value
adapters and runtimes remain replaceable realizations
hypotheses: stable typed meaning reduces reconstruction burden
exact source bindings and visible residue improve reviewability
deterministic package identity makes ontology changes safer to challenge
a project-owned contract makes ontology runtimes replaceable
counterevidence_routes: identity and validation overhead exceeds continuity value
a runtime becomes an irreplaceable meaning authority
revision_criteria: a realization repeatedly violates a first-order principle
the approach fails to preserve meaning continuity or project ownership
a materially simpler approach preserves the same guarantees
systemic counterevidence invalidates the value mechanism

revision_history.change: Created the Ontology Product as a CyberAlchemy subproduct and bound its draft thesis to one candidate Project and Goal.

challenge_route: Challenge product identity or thesis meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 product owner; challenge ontology evidence through the CyberAlchemy v2 ontology route; challenge Project or Goal lifecycle through their named owner route.
claim_ceiling: Draft product direction and candidate ontology foundation only; not product realization, outcome proof, Arcanum replacement, publication, release, deployment, or production authority.
